stops.note: to make warm, from calere (to be warm) and facere (to make)
to heat, from calefacere, later applied to the person who stoked an early steam-powered car's engine
one who heats, applied to the driver who operated the earliest motor cars
stops.meaning: a hired driver of a motor car

stops.note: French 'stoker', from early steam-powered cars whose drivers stoked the boiler
stops.meaning: a person employed to drive a private motor vehicle

current_meaning: a person employed to drive a private motor vehicle for someone else
